checks.invariant: No source-visible cap on how many grant rows one granter may write naming another sub or group: id
checks.result: grant_rows (rights.py:894-920) checks only lawful principal, level, and read_write at the addressed path (_grant_refusal 1305-1336). _lawful_principal accepts any non-reserved id, including any group: id. No per-principal, per-granter or per-mount row-count cap exists (searched for grant cap/limit/budget). The backend default posture is read_write at the root (backend.py:205), so under defaults anonymous can grant. The victim cannot revoke rows naming itself at paths where it lacks read_write.

checks.invariant: How the grantee's per-call cost scales with planted rows
checks.result: Every profiled dialect declares range_source, so Visibility.narrow (rights.py:541-551) uses visible_entries (ranges.py:96) as one statement for read, glob and the other narrowed verbs. That path does not fan out by statement count. The GENERIC floor has no range_source, so narrow fans out one statement per visibility_clauses clause for every read verb. The glean vector leg (glean.py:648-670) always calls view.clauses() and runs one statement per clause, on every dialect, up to two probe windows. visibility_clauses caps each clause at 200 units (arm_budget, dialects.py:666-676), so the clause count is about 2n/200 for n planted prefixes. Each statement stays inside the bind budget, but the number of statements per call grows without bound.

checks.invariant: Measured victim statements, compile time, call time and event-loop gap as planted rows grow
checks.result: InMemoryStorage, posture none at /, mallory read_write at /home/mallory, victim alice. The first 250 rows were planted through grant() as mallory (3.4-5.7 ms each); the rest were bulk-inserted as identical rows. Planted 250/1250/2500/5000: glob and read stayed at 4 statements warm and 8-10 cold; the cold compile took 1.0/4.7/10.3/26.4 ms and was redone after a single mallory grant (the stamp retires the cache entry). glean took 12/22/35/61 statements and made 3/13/26/52 clauses. Warm glean took 44/395/1267/2348 ms, and the largest event-loop gap was 17/133/187/455 ms. The statement count roughly doubles when n doubles.

checks.invariant: Whether meet minimal=True pruning has a work bound or offload
checks.result: graph_rows (graph.py:166-191) calls prune synchronously after meet_walk. prune (422-440) loops while minimal is set. Each iteration rebuilds _adjacency over all walk edges, reruns _articulation_points over the kept set, sorts the removable nodes, and removes only one node before calling _strip_leaves again. _strip_leaves rebuilds the adjacency once per leaf round (596-608). The source shows no budget, no deadline and no executor offload, so the work is about k*(V+E) for k removable nodes. backend.graph (403-447) validates only that depth and limit are at least 1 and checks the edge-type count. limit is applied in observe() after pruning.

unresolved: The growth ratio and event-loop stall of prune at n and 2n were not measured locally in this run. The quadratic-or-worse shape comes from source reading only. It needs a bounded measurement: count _adjacency and _articulation_points calls at two small graph sizes.

candidates.title: Uncapped grant rows naming another principal make that principal's glean issue a growing number of statements and stall the shared event loop
candidates.description: Any principal holding read_write at some path (anonymous everywhere under the default read_write root posture) can write any number of grant rows naming another sub or a group: id at distinct sub-paths. Every later call by the grantee (or by every member of the group) compiles all of those rows. The glean vector leg then runs one statement per visibility clause, about one per 100 planted rows. The rows persist, and the grantee cannot revoke them. Measured on InMemoryStorage: with 5000 planted rows a warm glean grew from 44 ms to 2.3 s and from 12 to 61 statements, and the event loop stalled for up to 455 ms per call. Each further grant also retires the grantee's RightsCache entry, which forces a fresh compile that grows with n.
candidates.root_cause: grant_rows/_grant_refusal impose no count bound on rows naming a principal other than the granter. The glean vector leg uses the per-clause fan from visibility_clauses (glean.py:648-670) instead of the single-statement range source, so the statement count grows with the grantee's piece count. The compile (Resolution.compile) and statement construction run on the event loop.
candidates.intended_behavior: A grantee's per-call cost should not grow without bound with rows another principal plants. Either cap the grant rows naming a principal (or per granter), or keep the vector leg's visibility pushdown at a statement count that is constant in the grantee's rights, as narrow() already does through visible_entries.

trace.description: Any caller with read_write at the path may grant any lawful principal, including another sub or a group: id
The gate checks only principal lawfulness, level and read_write at the path; there is no count cap. stamp_principals retires the grantee's cache
On a cache miss, the call reads every row naming the grantee's subjects and groups, then compiles them in Python
Splits the rights into OR-clauses of at most 200 units each, so the clause count grows linearly with planted prefixes
Runs one statement per clause (and per probe window) on every dialect

evidence.description: _lawful_principal accepts any non-reserved, non-blank id within the column length; no count check exists anywhere in the grant path
The default posture is read_write at the root, so under defaults anonymous passes the grant gate
narrow() uses the single-statement range source where the dialect has one; glean's vector leg does not, and the GENERIC floor fans out for all read verbs
arm_budget caps clause width at 200 units, which keeps each statement bounded while the statement count grows

conditions.description: The attacker holds read_write at some path. Under the default root posture this includes anonymous.

The attacker plants rows naming the victim sub or a group: id at distinct prefixes the victim does not otherwise cover. The victim must use glean (any dialect), or any read verb on the GENERIC floor, to see the statement fan.

execution.attacker_perspective: A principal with read_write on its own subtree grants read on many distinct sub-paths to a victim sub
payloads: for i in range(n): storage.grant(path=Path(f'/home/mallory/p{i:06d}'), principal='alice', level='read', authority=Authority.of(Principal('mallory')))
instructions: Create an InMemoryStorage, write 20 files owned by alice, set posture none at /, grant alice read_write on /home/alice and mallory read_write on /home/mallory as system
Plant 250 grants as mallory through grant(), then bulk-insert identical rows up to n
Count the statements alice's glob, read and glean calls issue, with a 1 ms asyncio ticker running, at n = 250, 1250, 2500 and 5000, inside the sandbox
execution.observed_result: glean took 12/22/35/61 statements and made 3/13/26/52 clauses. Warm glean took 44/395/1267/2348 ms, and the largest event-loop gap was 17/133/187/455 ms. glob and read stayed at a constant statement count, but their cold compile grew from 1.0 to 26.4 ms and a single mallory grant forced it again.

remediation.strategy: Route the glean vector leg's visibility through visible_entries (a join or a semi-join on the range source), as narrow() already does, so the statement count is constant in the grantee's rights. Separately, bound the number of grant rows naming one principal or written by one granter, or require the grantee's consent for rows that name it. Offload compiles above a size threshold.

likelihood.reason: It needs only read_write somewhere; the default posture grants that to anonymous. Planting is cheap (a few ms per grant), and the rows persist.

impact.reason: It degrades a chosen victim's (or a whole group's) glean persistently and linearly with planted rows, and the event-loop stalls affect every caller in the process. No data is disclosed.

confidence.reason: The growth was measured locally on SQLite only. The GENERIC fan-out for every read verb is source-derived, and real-engine timings were not observed.

hardening: RightsCache keeps the newest entry even when it alone exceeds the 64 MiB budget (rights.py:289-296). Very large grantee compiles therefore evict every other principal's entry; this was not measured at that scale.
The glean vector-leg statement with the owner arm reached about 7.5k OR terms in one statement on SQLite. It stays inside bind_cap, but the depth budget applies per unit, not to the whole statement.
